title: Lazard Asset Management Launches Its First Three Fixed Income ETFs, Providing Investors New Ways To Access Differentiated Income
summary: New York, November 9, 2026 – Lazard Asset Management (“LAM”) today announced its entry into fixed income ETFs with the launch of three actively managed strategies: Lazard US High Yield ETF (NYSE Arca: HYB), Lazard Hybrid Financial Income ETF (NYSE Arca: HYFY), and Lazard Non-Dollar Active Income ETF (NYSE Arca: XDLR). Each is managed by a specialized Lazard investment team and designed to give investors differentiated sources of income.
body_markdown:
**Lazard US High Yield ETF (NYSE Arca: HYB)** seeks maximum total return from a combination of capital appreciation and current income by investing primarily in below investment grade corporate bonds tied economically to the US. HYB converted from the Lazard US High Yield Portfolio, a mutual fund launched in 1995, and is expected to adopt the Portfolio’s performance history.


*Portfolio Manager Gordon McKemie said: “HYB is built around our highest-conviction ideas, chosen one bond at a time. It is higher quality, with fewer of the lowest-rated credits and more secured debt than in past cycles. Yields are meaningful and duration is short, so that income provides a cushion. But spreads are tight, so security selection matters more than market exposure. A proprietary screen helps us identify attractively valued credits, and our analysts underwrite each one in depth, building forward-looking scenarios rather than replaying past cycles.* HYB invests at least 80% of its assets in high yield fixed income securities and is expected to maintain an average weighted maturity of two to 10 years. The team assesses each credit on its own merits and deviates from the benchmark only where it expects to be paid for the risk, with avoiding permanent loss of capital as its first priority. The fund is managed by **Gordon McKemie** , **John Senesac** , and **Kyle Lanphear** , a portfolio management team averaging more than 25 years of investment experience.
